accepted.s: Under the Disaster Management Act, 2005, the National Disaster Response Fund is constituted under which section?
accepted.x: The National Disaster Response Fund is constituted under Section 46 of the Disaster Management Act, 2005.
accepted.tq: Use the exact statutory-section distinction among closely related disaster funds.
accepted.sec: Disaster funds - NDRF, SDRF, mitigation funds, Finance Commission

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF)?
o: It is a fund maintained jointly by PRIs and district administrations
It provides long-term financing exclusively for mitigation projects
It is the first fund used by every State for all local disasters
It is a Central fund that tops up the SDRF during severe calamities
accepted.x: The NDRF is a Central fund used to supplement or top up the State Disaster Response Fund during severe calamities.
accepted.tq: Distinguish response funding from long-term mitigation funding.
accepted.sec: Disaster funds - NDRF, SDRF, mitigation funds, Finance Commission

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF):
1. It is constituted under Section 48 of the Disaster Management Act, 2005.
2. It is the first fund available for relief in notified disasters.
3. In general States, the Centre-State contribution ratio is 75:25.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: the SDRF is associated with Section 48, serves as the first relief fund for notified disasters, and has a 75:25 Centre-State contribution ratio for general States.
accepted.tq: Check each fund against its section, purpose and financing ratio.
accepted.sec: Disaster funds - NDRF, SDRF, mitigation funds, Finance Commission

accepted.s: The National and State Disaster Mitigation Funds are primarily intended for which purpose?
o: Payment of compensation to members of response forces
Immediate relief in notified disasters only
Financing only post-disaster reconstruction of roads
accepted.x: The National and State Disaster Mitigation Funds are intended for long-term risk reduction and mitigation rather than immediate relief alone.
accepted.tq: Apply the relief-versus-mitigation distinction.
accepted.sec: Disaster funds - NDRF, SDRF, mitigation funds, Finance Commission

accepted.s: The National and State Disaster Mitigation Funds are associated with which section of the Disaster Management Act, 2005?
accepted.x: The National and State Disaster Mitigation Funds are associated with Section 47 of the Disaster Management Act, 2005.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the adjacent statutory sections for response and mitigation funds.
accepted.sec: Disaster funds - NDRF, SDRF, mitigation funds, Finance Commission

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Finance Commission and disaster funds is correct?
o: It directly notifies every disaster eligible for relief funding.
It recommends the calamities to be covered and the amount allocated to each State, while the Ministry of Home Affairs notifies them.
It manages the State Emergency Operations Centres of all States.
It fixes the contribution ratio of every State without reference to any guidelines.
accepted.x: The Finance Commission recommends the calamities covered and the allocation for each State; the Ministry of Home Affairs subsequently notifies them.
accepted.tq: Use the ‘who recommends and who notifies’ authority trap.
accepted.sec: Disaster funds - NDRF, SDRF, mitigation funds, Finance Commission

accepted.s: Under the provision concerning State-specific local disasters, a State may use up to what percentage of its SDRF?
accepted.x: States may use up to 10% of the SDRF for State-specific local disasters.
accepted.tq: Test the precise percentage rather than the general purpose of the fund.
accepted.sec: Disaster funds - NDRF, SDRF, mitigation funds, Finance Commission

accepted.s: An allocation of Rs 4,645 crore was approved for National Disaster Mitigation Fund projects covering how many States, including Andhra Pradesh?
accepted.x: National Disaster Mitigation Fund projects worth Rs 4,645 crore were approved for nine States, including Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Separate the project amount from the number of beneficiary States.
accepted.sec: Disaster funds - NDRF, SDRF, mitigation funds, Finance Commission

accepted.s: The acronym ‘NDRF’ in disaster management may refer to which two distinct entities?
o: National District Relief Force and National Disaster Rehabilitation Fund
National Disaster Recovery Framework and National Development Resilience Fund
National Disaster Response Force and National Disaster Response Fund
National Disaster Relief Framework and National Development Response Fund
accepted.x: NDRF denotes both the National Disaster Response Force and the National Disaster Response Fund, depending on the context.
accepted.tq: Resolve an acronym trap by identifying the Force–Fund pair.
accepted.sec: Disaster funds - NDRF, SDRF, mitigation funds, Finance Commission

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding international disaster-risk-reduction frameworks:

List-I (Framework)
a. IDNDR
b. Hyogo Framework for Action
c. Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction
d. CDRI

List-II (Period or launch year)
i. 2015–2030
ii. 1990–1999
iii. Launched in 2019
iv. 2005–2015

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
accepted.x: IDNDR covered 1990–1999, Hyogo covered 2005–2015, Sendai covers 2015–2030, and CDRI was launched in 2019.
accepted.tq: Start with the distinctive CDRI launch year and verify the remaining periods.
accepted.sec: International frameworks - IDNDR, Hyogo, Sendai targets, CDRI

accepted.s: Which of the following is the correct chronological order of the major international disaster-risk-reduction frameworks or initiatives?
accepted.x: The chronological order is IDNDR (1990–1999), Hyogo (2005–2015), Sendai (2015–2030), and CDRI, launched in 2019.
accepted.tq: Fix the first and last items before arranging the middle frameworks.
accepted.sec: International frameworks - IDNDR, Hyogo, Sendai targets, CDRI

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the relationship between the Hyogo Framework for Action and the Sendai Framework?
o: Hyogo was the predecessor of Sendai.
Sendai was the predecessor of Hyogo.
Hyogo was the successor to Sendai.
Both were launched in the same year and cover the same period.
accepted.x: The Hyogo Framework for Action for 2005–2015 preceded and was succeeded by the Sendai Framework for 2015–2030.
accepted.tq: Test predecessor–successor direction in a paired framework question.
accepted.sec: International frameworks - IDNDR, Hyogo, Sendai targets, CDRI

accepted.s:
With reference to the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction, consider the following statements:
1. It covers the period 2015–2030.
2. It contains four priorities for action.
3. It contains seven global targets.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Sendai Framework covers 2015–2030 and contains four priorities and seven global targets.
accepted.tq: Combine the framework’s period with its two key numerical features.
accepted.sec: International frameworks - IDNDR, Hyogo, Sendai targets, CDRI

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT one of the four priorities of the Sendai Framework?
o: Investing in disaster-risk reduction for resilience
Replacing all community-based systems with centralised response agencies
accepted.x: The four priorities include understanding risk, strengthening risk governance, investing in risk reduction, and enhancing preparedness for effective response and Build Back Better. Replacing community systems is not a Sendai priority.
accepted.tq: Find the option that does not belong to the recognised priority set.
accepted.sec: International frameworks - IDNDR, Hyogo, Sendai targets, CDRI

accepted.s: The Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure (CDRI) is best described as:
o: A predecessor framework to the Hyogo Framework for Action
A UN treaty body headquartered in Geneva
An India-led infrastructure-resilience coalition with its secretariat in New Delhi
A State-level fund administered by the Ministry of Home Affairs
accepted.x: CDRI is an India-led coalition focused on infrastructure resilience, and its secretariat is located in New Delhi.
accepted.tq: Combine the organisation’s identity, leadership and headquarters.
accepted.sec: International frameworks - IDNDR, Hyogo, Sendai targets, CDRI

accepted.s: The short-, medium- and long-term time frames under the NDMP 2016 are respectively:
accepted.x: The NDMP 2016 provided short-term, medium-term and long-term time frames of five, ten and fifteen years respectively.
accepted.tq: Test the ordered duration sequence rather than a single date.
accepted.sec: National Policy on DM 2009, NDMP 2016 phases, APSDMA structure

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes APSDMA?
o: It is a district-level body headed by the District Collector.
It is an international coalition for infrastructure resilience.
It is a temporary relief committee constituted after a major disaster.
It is the apex statutory State body for disaster-management policy and plans, and it runs the State Emergency Operations Centre and early warning functions.
accepted.x: APSDMA is the apex statutory State body for disaster-management policy and plans and is responsible for the State Emergency Operations Centre and early warning functions.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the State apex authority from district and international bodies.
accepted.sec: National Policy on DM 2009, NDMP 2016 phases, APSDMA structure

accepted.s: The Andhra Pradesh Disaster Management Rules under which APSDMA is chaired by the Chief Minister were made in:
accepted.x: The Andhra Pradesh Disaster Management Rules were made in 2007.
accepted.tq: Separate the State rules year from the Act, policy and plan years.
accepted.sec: National Policy on DM 2009, NDMP 2016 phases, APSDMA structure

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the community-based disaster risk reduction programme through PRIs:
1. It is jointly run by the Ministry of Panchayati Raj and NDMA.
2. It covers 20 States and 81 districts.
3. It covers 20 Gram Panchayats in each district.
4. It includes 20 model Gram Panchayats.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. The programme is jointly run by MoPR and NDMA, covers 20 States and 81 districts, includes 20 Gram Panchayats per district, and has 20 model Gram Panchayats.
accepted.tq: Track each numerical coverage detail instead of treating the programme as a general PRIs initiative.
accepted.sec: National Policy on DM 2009, NDMP 2016 phases, APSDMA structure

accepted.s: What is the sanctioned amount associated with the community-based disaster risk reduction programme through PRIs?
accepted.x: The community-based disaster risk reduction programme through PRIs involves Rs 507.37 crore.
accepted.tq: Test the exact financial figure attached to the programme.
accepted.sec: National Policy on DM 2009, NDMP 2016 phases, APSDMA structure

accepted.s: Heatwaves and lightning were added to India’s notified disaster list, increasing the number of categories from:
accepted.x: The addition of heatwaves and lightning increased the notified disaster categories from 12 to 14.
accepted.tq: Use the before-and-after count to identify the policy change.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: The addition of heatwaves and lightning to the notified disaster list primarily enables access to:
accepted.x: Their inclusion in the notified list opens the possibility of support from the SDRF, NDRF and disaster mitigation funds.
accepted.tq: Link a policy classification change to its funding consequence.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: The ‘Resilient India 2047’ initiative of NDMA asks Union Ministries to prepare plans under which provisions of the Disaster Management Act?
accepted.x: The initiative asks Union Ministries to prepare plans under Sections 35 and 37 of the Disaster Management Act.
accepted.tq: Match the initiative with the exact statutory provisions.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which of the following is identified as a criticism or continuing challenge in India’s disaster-management system?
o: Excessive emphasis on mitigation expenditure over relief
Outdated India Disaster Resource Network data
Universal constitution of SDRFs in every State
Complete multi-hazard mapping across the country
accepted.x: The India Disaster Resource Network inventory is described as outdated. Other identified challenges include incomplete multi-hazard mapping, SDRFs not being raised in all States, and relief-centric spending.
accepted.tq: Select the genuine system deficiency among reversed or exaggerated claims.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which proposal has been suggested to improve comparative assessment of disaster vulnerability among States?
o: A biennial National Relief Expenditure Census
An annual NDMA State Disaster Vulnerability Index
accepted.x: A proposal has been made for an annual NDMA State Disaster Vulnerability Index.
accepted.tq: Identify the specific institutional proposal rather than a generic reform.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the City Flood Alert initiative in Andhra Pradesh:
1. It is associated with RTGS, APSDMA and IIT Gandhinagar.
2. It provides warnings up to 48 hours for rain and six hours for flash floods.
3. Vijayawada was the first city covered by the initiative.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The City Flood Alert initiative involves RTGS, APSDMA and IIT Gandhinagar, provides 48-hour rain and six-hour flash-flood warnings, and began with Vijayawada.
accepted.tq: Combine institutional partners, warning horizons and pilot location.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Bay of Bengal low-pressure systems and Andhra Pradesh is correct?
o: Andhra Pradesh receives 2–3 such systems annually, mainly from the Arabian Sea.
It receives 30–35 such systems annually, exclusively from the southern Bay of Bengal.
Such systems affect only the coastal districts and never the river basins.
It receives 13–14 such systems annually, mostly from the northern Bay of Bengal, affecting the Godavari and Krishna basins.
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh is associated with 13–14 Bay of Bengal low-pressure systems annually, mostly from the northern Bay, which can flood the Godavari and Krishna basins.
accepted.tq: Check the frequency, source region and affected basins together.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: The NIDM Southern Campus mentioned in the Andhra Pradesh disaster-management context is located at:
accepted.x: The Southern Campus of the National Institute of Disaster Management is located at Kondapalli.
accepted.tq: Discriminate the institutional location from nearby operational centres.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents Andhra Pradesh’s allocations under disaster-related funds for the years mentioned?
o: Rs 277.63 crore in 2026–27 and Rs 479.01 crore in 2025–26
Rs 479.01 crore under SDMF/NDMF in 2025–26 and Rs 521.17 crore under SDRF/NDRF in 2026–27
Rs 277.63 crore under SDRF/NDRF in 2025–26 and Rs 479.01 crore in 2026–27
Rs 521.17 crore under SDRF/NDRF in 2025–26 and Rs 277.63 crore under SDMF/NDMF in 2026–27
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh released Rs 277.63 crore in 2025–26 and Rs 479.01 crore in 2026–27 under SDRF/NDRF; Rs 521.17 crore was allocated under SDMF/NDMF.
accepted.tq: Match each amount with its year and funding category.
accepted.sec: Universal angles
